support: Every week of rain through that roof works further into the bottom of the stack, and I doubt October will come soon enough for the two Gates.
If the vote goes against them, or simply comes too late, forty-one years of Marrow's lettering could leave the depot in a skip.
WV12-P01.5.note: The author's only first-person statements look ahead to the boards' destruction by rain or scrapping, which is concern for their fate rather than praise, criticism, humor, or nostalgia.

WV12-P02.5.note: The narrator laughs at the swarm on the clothesline and still grins at the memory, and the hives are ongoing rather than lost, so amusement fits and wistfulness does not.

support: On every windy night since the storm I have lain awake listening for the sound of falling brick from the hill, and each morning I look out to see whether the chimney is still standing.
If the vote goes the other way, or a winter gale finds the crack first, the swifts will come back in May to an empty patch of sky above a heap of brick.
